title: Stormlord
build: The Bonanza Crew Stormlord +++ D64, trainers declined

tools.emulator: vice-mcp v3.14.0 macOS arm64 headless, dummy audio

exclude: KERNAL screen before startup. $C105 builds the two pixel lookup pages there.
Second VIC bank sprite work area. Startup watchpoints measured 5,888 writes and zero CPU reads before completing the copy from $C500–$DBFF.
KERNAL workspace at entry. $C0F6 copies the 512 timer asset bytes from $7860–$7A5F.
Runtime per-column table. The hand-over has the KERNAL screen fill. Watchpoints through initial level drawing show 224 stores to this range.
Title workspace. Entry-to-$3F5C watchpoints counted 636 writes and zero reads, as $3F35 copied the title asset pages from beneath I/O.
Title screen matrix. The first clear at $3324 writes all 1,024 cells, with no earlier CPU read measured.
Generated per-tile top-left screen colors written by $E000 from the source records at $6000.
Generated per-tile top-right screen colors written by $E000 from the source records at $6000.
Generated per-tile bottom-left screen colors written by $E000 from the source records at $6000.
Generated per-tile bottom-right screen colors written by $E000 from the source records at $6000.
Generated per-tile left color nibbles written by $E000 from the source records at $6000.
Generated per-tile right color nibbles written by $E000 from the source records at $6000.
Expanded map workspace. Watches through the first title decode saw 2,048 writes in $7E00–$85FF and 13 in $7DF3–$7DFF, with zero reads in either range.
Gameplay bitmap workspace above the panel. Checkpoints from the hand-over through the first $388C return saw zero CPU reads, and the renderer writes the visible cells from the resident tile records.
Alternate VIC screen cells generated by the tile drawing routines and shifted by $2B1F.
Alternate VIC screen rows filled by $2B1F. Through the first level draw, checkpoints counted 239 stores and zero reads in $42D0–$43BF.
Startup clears this page-sized area before installing the RAM interrupt vectors. Later timer writes generate its sprite contents.
The two CPU port registers and the zero-page workspace that startup clears before calling game routines.
Generated map object-list workspace. All bytes are $FF in the hand-over, and $3104 and $34B8 reinitialize the list terminator.
Runtime sprite position, color, pointer and queue tables maintained by the object and raster handlers.
Tile-redraw queue workspace, initially filled with $FF. $2F11 resets the first terminator.
The map command and object lookup tables generated by $3616 and $364C.
Runtime five-byte map command list. Initialized to its $FF sentinel by $3107 and filled by the object marker scanner.
Tile bitmap lookup workspace, zero at entry. Startup writes its pixel quadrants from the authored source at $6000.
The two tile bitmap pointer arrays. The hand-over is zero and startup constructs their values from the $8600 base, stride and shared-tile overrides.
Gameplay and renderer variables under the KERNAL, including the score, timer position, object limit and raster handshake.
Screen matrix workspace between the startup paths. From the hand-over through the first level draw, it received twelve stores and no CPU reads.
Generated bitmap cells beyond the authored panel color source. The first draw wrote all seventeen bytes and recorded no CPU reads.
Transient round and flight flags in the tail of the bitmap area. Startup initializes these addresses before the round loop reads them.
include: Authored VIC sprite pixels in RAM below I/O. Startup mirrors them to the other VIC bank.
Authored title graphics and display tables in RAM. $3F35 copies these pages to $E000.

io: The caller banks out I/O before this asset copy.
The caller banks out I/O before this asset copy.
The Hall of Fame highlight also writes its source raster data with I/O banked out.
